daily.title: Dollar lingers near 22-month peak as AI worries simmer
daily.summary: TOKYO, Nov 27 (Reuters) - The US dollar hovered below a 22-month peak in holiday-thinned trading on Friday, with traders looking to equity markets for clues on direction as doubts about the AI trade triggers heightened volatility. The dollar index, which measures the currency against a basket of six peers, was steady at 103.81, at the end of a week that saw it pop to the highest level since March of last year at 104.53 on Monday only to erase those gains a day later. For the week, the index is currently flat.

daily.title: Australian shares set for best week since August as financials, WiseTech rally
daily.summary: Nov 27 (Reuters) - Australian shares edged higher on Friday and were on track for their best week since early August, buoyed by financials and WiseTech Global after the software firm reaffirmed its annual revenue targets. The S&P/ASX 200 index was up 0.4% at 8,796.2 points, as of 2320 GMT. The benchmark has gained 2.4% so far this week, slowly recovering from a 5% decline last week, its worst showing since June 2022. Financials gained 0.5% and were set for a 1.1% weekly rise. National Australia Bank and ANZ Group were the only "Big Four" banks in positive territory.

daily.title: Senior Citizen Tax Rates For Tax Year 2026-27: With Example on Different Income Levels
daily.summary: Senior citizens in India can pay tax under two systems: the New Regime and the Old Regime.For Tax Year 2026–27, the New Regime has the same slabs for ever This guide compares the two in simple steps, so you can pick the one that saves you more tax. Tax Year 2026–27 is the same period as FY 2026–27 (AY 2027–28) under the older terminology. Tax is progressive, so each rate applies only to the income inside its band. A 4% Health and Education Cess is added on top, and a surcharge applies at higher incomes.

daily.title: Supreme Court to decide if duty-free goods must follow Indian domestic regulations
daily.summary: Counsel for the petitioner, Shyam Divan, argued that this interpretation creates a dangerous precedent for the entire travel retail industry The Supreme Court of India has issued a notice regarding a petition filed by Mumbai Travel Retail Private Limited, challenging a Bombay High Court ruling that could redefine the legal status of goods sold at duty-free outlets. At the core of the dispute is whether products stored and sold beyond the customs frontier are subject to domestic regulatory laws, or if they remain exempt until they enter the Domestic Tariff Area (DTA).

daily.title: Customs & Excise Duty Remission Allowed on EOU Goods Destroyed in Accidental Fire: CESTAT Ahmedabad

On 03.04.2010, a major fire occurred at its factory premises, destroying raw materials, inputs, work-in-progress, finished goods, capital goods, plant and machinery. The incident was intimated to the Department on 05.04.2010.

daily.summary: The CBIC has amended the CGST Rules to provide for automatic electronic cancellation of GST registration from December 1, 2026. daily.title: 47th Half-Yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves: April – September 2026
daily.summary: It may be recalled that in February 2004 , the Reserve Bank initiated the practice of compiling half-yearly reports on the management of foreign exchange reserves and making them public to promote greater transparency and enhance disclosure in the management of the country’s foreign exchange reserves. In this connection, Reserve Bank of India has today released the 47th Half-Yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves with reference to end-September 2026. During April-September 2026, India’s foreign exchange reserves increased from US$ 691.11 billion to US$ 737.78 billion.

breaking.title: NBFCs' dependence on bank borrowings needs monitoring over possible systemic concerns: RBI
breaking.summary: The Reserve Bank of India highlights the growing reliance of non-banking financial companies on bank borrowings, urging for continuous monitoring and diversification of funding to manage systemic risks. Rising dependence of non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) on bank borrowings needs to be monitored on an ongoing basis in view of possible systemic concerns , according to an article in the Reserve Bank of India's November Bulletin. Diversification of NBFCs' funding profile is imperative as their reliance on bank borrowings increases, it said. The borrowing profile of NBFCs has undergone a shift in recent years, driven by increasing reliance on banks.

breaking.title: Credit Card Spending Jumps 20% In October To Rs 2.45 Lakh Cr: RBI
breaking.summary: Transaction volumes grow faster, increasing 31.8 per cent over the same period Credit card transactions in India gathered pace in October, with total spending climbing to Rs 2.45 lakh crore, as festive-season purchases and increased payment activity drove a sharp month-on-month rise, according to the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) latest payment data. The value of credit card transactions increased 20.1 per cent from Rs 2.04 lakh crore in September. On a year-on-year basis, spending rose 14.4 per cent from Rs 2.14 lakh crore recorded in October 2025. Transaction volumes grew faster, increasing 31.8 per cent over the same period.
